Guidance & outlook: Going forward, yes, like ammonia, as you said, we were in the region of about INR50 a kg and now we are over INR100 a kg.
We expect that the next year will be like a normal year, which is about 5% to 10% growth rate, but there is too much uncertainty in the future.
That is what we expect that the country will be growing anyway at 5%, 7%, and we grow along with it.
Growth & demand: It's been basically flat volume and value, plus-minus 1% either way prices have dropped 1% and volume has probably dropped 1%.
So there is no question of ethylamines we have -- I mean, ethylamines, we have enough capacity for the next 4 to 5 years, assuming that the growth is natural in this 5% and 10%, which we see.
But in volume growth, it will be between 5% and 10%.
Margins & costs: On an average, we must be having between 60% and 85% capacity utilization, and that we continue to get enough raw material to keep there.
So it's fairly easy for the government to allocate 0.05% which is a critical raw material going into agricultural inputs to drugs.
But as I said earlier that most of our plants are between 60% to 85% capacity utilization.
Capex & expansion: And as you would be aware, we had informed the stock exchange both about the issues we have had with sourcing ammonia in March and subsequently, how we have been able to manage to keep the plants running.

But now that we have 4 players in methylamine in the country, we expect there will be competition in methyl because now Aarti has also commissioned their plant, and therefore, they expect to be some competition.
There's always some maintenance capex, INR20 crores, INR30 crores, something like that.
Risks & challenges: These statements are not the guarantee of future performance and involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict.
So we have had a few challenges in March in operations, but we have, by and large, overcome it.
